battery_100.name: Kings 100Ah Lithium Battery
battery_100.why: The cheapest well-known 100Ah, and you can pick one up in store almost anywhere.
battery_100.downside: Only a 1-year warranty and no app. It's often on sale for much less, so wait for a deal.

battery_100.name: VoltX 100Ah Lithium Battery
battery_100.why: Similar money to the Kings, bought online, with a longer warranty.
battery_100.downside: Online only, and the warranty wording on the listing is unclear, so check it before you buy.

battery_100.name: iTechworld iTECH120X PRO 120Ah
battery_100.why: An extra 20Ah, a phone app and a 5-year Aussie warranty for not much more than budget.
battery_100.downside: No heater, so it won't charge in freezing weather.

battery_100.name: Renogy 100Ah Pro (self-heating)
battery_100.why: Pick this if you camp somewhere frosty. It warms itself up before charging.

battery_100.name: REDARC REDLAB Icon 100Ah
battery_100.why: Australian brand with a built-in heater, a 5-year warranty and a charge display on the battery. Made to pair with REDARC chargers.
battery_100.downside: About three to four times the price of budget packs for the same usable power.

battery_100.name: Enerdrive eLITE 100Ah
battery_100.why: A respected caravan-industry brand for well under REDARC money.

battery_200.name: Kings 200Ah Lithium Battery
battery_200.why: Easy to buy in store, and people who've opened one up say it's decent inside for the money.
battery_200.downside: Kings prices swing a lot (it has been around $400 on sale), so watch for a deal before you buy.

battery_200.name: Renogy Reserve Mini 200Ah
battery_200.why: Ticks every box: built-in heater, phone app, strong 205A output and a 5-year warranty. Compact and light for 200Ah.
battery_200.downside: Online only, and on pre-order until November. The iTechworld 200Ah slim is a good in-stock alternative.

battery_200.name: iTechworld iTECH200SS Super Slim
battery_200.why: Phone app, a strong 200A output and a 5-year Aussie warranty, in a slim 12.6cm shape that fits a van wall or under a seat. In stock.
battery_200.downside: No heater, so it won't charge in freezing weather. The Renogy below has one.

battery_200.name: REDARC REDLAB Icon 200Ah
battery_200.why: Australian-designed, heated, and the 5-year warranty covers work use too.
battery_200.downside: About three times the mid-range price.

battery_200.name: Enerdrive B-TEC 200Ah Gen2
battery_200.why: A long-time favourite of caravan builders, with app monitoring.
battery_200.downside: No heater, and it can take 2 to 3 weeks to arrive.

battery_400.name: 2 × Kings 200Ah Lithium
battery_400.why: The cheapest way to about 400Ah from a store you can walk into.
battery_400.downside: No app or heater, and you'll need link cables. Much cheaper on sale.

battery_400.name: iTechworld iTECH400X PRO 400Ah
battery_400.why: One battery, one set of terminals, a phone app and 5 years' cover. Simpler than linking two.
battery_400.downside: 38kg in one lump is hard to lift into place, and there's no heater.

battery_400.name: 2 × Renogy Reserve Mini 200Ah
battery_400.why: Heated, and split into two 20kg pieces that are easier to carry and fit.
battery_400.downside: Needs link cables and an auto electrician to join them.

battery_400.name: Enerdrive B-TEC 400Ah bundle (2 × 200Ah)
battery_400.why: A proven caravan-grade brand, sold as a matched pair with the link cables.
battery_400.downside: Special order and can't be returned. No heater.

battery_400.name: 2 × REDARC REDLAB Icon 200Ah
battery_400.why: The top choice for charging in freezing weather and an all-REDARC system.

powerbox_100.name: Kings BatBlock25 with 100Ah Lithium
powerbox_100.why: Battery, 25A DC-DC, solar input, plugs and USB-C in one box, with a 7m lead to your car battery included.
powerbox_100.downside: Right now it costs more than our mid-range pick, so only buy it on sale.

powerbox_100.name: iTechworld GoFurther box with 120Ah PRO
powerbox_100.why: Best value: a faster 40A charger, solar input, a battery monitor, phone app and a 5-year battery warranty.
powerbox_100.downside: Stock comes and goes, so check it's available.

powerbox_100.name: iTechworld GoFurther box with 100Ah
powerbox_100.why: The same box, if the 120Ah version is sold out.
powerbox_100.downside: Smaller battery, no app and a shorter warranty for about the same price.

powerbox_100.name: REDARC GoBlock 100Ah
powerbox_100.why: Top Australian build with a 50A charger, 50A solar regulator and full app control. Charges much faster.
powerbox_100.downside: About three and a half times the iTechworld price, with a 2-year warranty.

dcdc_25.name: Kings 25A DC-DC Charger
dcdc_25.why: The cheapest way to charge a lithium battery from both your engine and solar, with plug-in leads.
dcdc_25.downside: Kings don't publish the warranty or solar limits, so ask in store.

dcdc_25.name: Renogy 30A DC-DC with MPPT
dcdc_25.why: A bit more charging (30A) for similar money.

dcdc_25.name: REDARC BCDC Core 25A
dcdc_25.why: Australian REDARC quality, works with smart alternators, and almost every auto electrician knows it.
dcdc_25.downside: Mounts inside the car only, not under the bonnet. No app.

dcdc_25.name: Projecta IDC25X 25A
dcdc_25.why: Fully waterproof, can go under the bonnet, and has a 5-year warranty. Also at BCF.
dcdc_25.downside: The app needs an extra display you buy separately.

dcdc_25.name: REDARC BCDC Alpha 25A
dcdc_25.why: Top-end REDARC with phone app control and solar priority, so it uses the sun before your alternator.
dcdc_25.downside: About double the Core for the same 25A of charging.

dcdc_25.name: REDARC BCDC Classic 25A
dcdc_25.why: The long-proven REDARC that can live under the bonnet.
dcdc_25.downside: No app, and it costs more than the Projecta.

dcdc_40.name: Renogy 40A DC-DC with MPPT
dcdc_40.why: Very cheap for 40A with solar built in.
dcdc_40.downside: Only takes small 12V-style panels (25V max), not big house-style panels.

dcdc_40.name: iTechworld 40A DC-DC
dcdc_40.why: Takes a wider range of panels than the Renogy and handles smart alternators.

dcdc_40.name: Kings 40A DC-DC Charger
dcdc_40.why: Easy to buy in store, and it plugs straight into Kings batteries and leads.
dcdc_40.downside: Costs more than the Renogy and iTechworld, and specs aren't published.

dcdc_40.name: REDARC BCDC Core 40A
dcdc_40.why: Brand-name reliability that every installer knows, at a fair price for 40A.
dcdc_40.downside: Mounts inside the car only, no app.

dcdc_40.name: REDARC BCDC Core 40A Quick Connect
dcdc_40.why: Plug-in connectors make the install simpler.
dcdc_40.downside: Same limits as the standard Core.

dcdc_40.name: Enerdrive DC2DC 40A + MPPT
dcdc_40.why: Takes up to 800W of solar and has a 5-year warranty, so you can grow your panels later. A screen shows what it's doing.

dcdc_40.name: REDARC BCDC Classic 40A
dcdc_40.why: The pick if the charger has to sit in the engine bay.
dcdc_40.downside: No app, and dearer than the Enerdrive.

dcdc_50.name: Renogy 50A DC-DC with MPPT
dcdc_50.why: The cheapest 50A with solar and a phone app, and it takes bigger panels (up to 50V).
dcdc_50.downside: Shops price it quite differently, so compare before you buy.

dcdc_50.name: Projecta IDC50X 50A
dcdc_50.why: 5-year warranty and up to 800W of solar, so it suits a roof full of panels.
dcdc_50.downside: The app needs an extra display.

dcdc_50.name: REDARC BCDC Classic 50A
dcdc_50.downside: No app, and only about $130 less than the Alpha.

dcdc_50.name: REDARC BCDC Alpha 50A
dcdc_50.why: App control, solar priority to go easy on your alternator, and it takes bigger panels (up to 48V).

dcdc_50.name: REDARC Alpha 50 with Smart Battery Monitor
dcdc_50.why: Charger and an accurate battery monitor in one matched kit, all in one app.
dcdc_50.downside: About $300 more than an Alpha plus a Victron SmartShunt bought separately.

dcdc_50.name: Victron Orion XS 50A (no solar input)
dcdc_50.why: An excellent, efficient charger with a built-in app, if you're going all Victron.
dcdc_50.downside: No solar input. You'd need a separate solar controller as well.

blanket_200.name: Kings 240W Solar Blanket + 6m lead
blanket_200.why: Cheapest way into a decent-sized blanket. No regulator inside, which suits a DC-DC charger that does the regulating.
blanket_200.downside: Kings quality is mixed, and the price changes almost daily.

blanket_200.name: Hard Korr 200W Solar Blanket
blanket_200.why: An Aussie brand with a regulator you can unplug. Leave it off when you plug into a DC-DC charger.
blanket_200.downside: The built-in regulator is the basic type, so feed it through your DC-DC. Snowys is pickup only right now.

blanket_200.name: iTechworld 200W Solar Blanket
blanket_200.why: Tough outer cover and good local support.
blanket_200.downside: Heavier than the Hard Korr, with a 1-year warranty.

blanket_200.name: REDARC 160W Solar Blanket
blanket_200.why: Australian-made quality with a genuine Anderson plug, built to plug into a REDARC charger, and backed by ARB stores everywhere.
blanket_200.downside: About four times the Kings per watt, for fewer watts.

roof_200.name: Kings 200W Fixed Glass Panel
roof_200.why: About 75c a watt. Add a Kings 100W ($134) for 300W.
roof_200.downside: Heavy for the watts, and quality control is mixed.

roof_200.name: Renogy 200W Mono Panel
roof_200.why: Well-known brand, 5-year warranty, and a long narrow shape that suits van roofs.

roof_200.name: Victron 190W Mono Panel
roof_200.why: A premium brand for about $1 a watt.

roof_200.name: REDARC 200W Black Frame Panel
roof_200.why: Australian brand that ARB stores sell and fit. Pairs neatly with a REDARC charger.
roof_200.downside: About $2 a watt, with a shorter warranty than Renogy.

roof_200.name: Sunman eArc 200W Flexible Panel
roof_200.why: Light, glass-free and low profile, for curved roofs or pop-tops.
roof_200.downside: Flexible panels run hotter stuck flat to a roof.

roof_600.name: 3 × Kings 200W Fixed Glass Panels
roof_600.why: The cheapest real 600W, leaving more money for the battery.
roof_600.downside: About 35kg on the roof before brackets, and three may not fit a mid-size van.

roof_600.name: 3 × Renogy 200W Mono Panels
roof_600.why: 5-year warranty, and the narrow shape lies across a van roof more easily.

roof_600.name: 3 × Victron 190W Mono Panels
roof_600.why: A premium brand for less than the Renogy setup.

roof_600.name: 3 × REDARC 200W Black Frame Panels
roof_600.why: A one-brand REDARC system with ARB fitting and support across Australia.
roof_600.downside: Nearly three times the budget price for the same watts.

roof_600.name: 3 × Sunman eArc 200W Flexible Panels
roof_600.why: The lightweight way to 600W, far less weight than glass.
roof_600.downside: Needs proper mounting with airflow underneath.

inverter_600.name: Jaycar 500W Pure Sine Inverter
inverter_600.why: Small, light and cheap, from a store with branches everywhere. Plenty for laptops and camera chargers.
inverter_600.downside: Being replaced by a newer model, so stock may run out.

inverter_600.name: Victron Phoenix 12/800
inverter_600.why: Top-quality brand and a 5-year warranty, for less than most mid-range brands.
inverter_600.downside: It's rated 800VA, which is about 650W of real output.

inverter_600.name: Projecta IP600 600W
inverter_600.why: Comes with a remote display and wiring kit, and it's easy to find at car-parts stores.
inverter_600.downside: Costs more than the Victron, which is better built.

inverter_600.name: Enerdrive ePOWER 600W
inverter_600.why: Australian RV specialist, 5-year warranty, compact at 2kg. A safety-switch (RCD) version is available.
inverter_600.downside: Handles smaller start-up surges than the Victron.

inverter_2000.name: Renogy 2000W Pure Sine (with UPS)
inverter_2000.why: A known brand at a budget price. Switches to campsite power by itself when you plug in.
inverter_2000.downside: Warranty isn't listed, so ask before buying.

inverter_2000.name: Hard Korr 2000W Pure Sine
inverter_2000.why: Aussie brand with a 2-year replacement warranty, light at 3kg, and stocked at Supercheap.

inverter_2000.name: iTechworld 2000W Pure Sine
inverter_2000.why: Good local support, often bundled with their batteries.
inverter_2000.downside: 1-year warranty and heavier than the Hard Korr.

inverter_2000.name: Enerdrive ePOWER 2000W
inverter_2000.why: Built for RVs to run coffee machines and hairdryers day after day, with a 5-year warranty. RCD versions available.
inverter_2000.downside: About two and a half times the Hard Korr.

inverter_2000.name: Victron Phoenix 12/2000 Smart
inverter_2000.why: Top build quality with a built-in app, ideal in a full Victron system.
inverter_2000.downside: Rated 2000VA, about 1,600W real output. Was sold out when we checked.

monitor.name: Kings 500A Battery Monitor
monitor.why: A wired screen showing your real battery percentage and power in and out, for about $100.
monitor.downside: No app, and no warranty listed.

monitor.name: iTechworld BM500 Monitor
monitor.why: Same job and price from an Aussie lithium specialist.

monitor.name: Renogy 500A Battery Monitor
monitor.why: Well reviewed, with low-battery alarms. Also at Supercheap.

monitor.name: Victron SmartShunt 500A
monitor.why: The accuracy and app installers trust, for only about $40 more than budget. Shows hours left on your phone.
monitor.downside: No wall screen, your phone is the display. Mount it somewhere dry.

monitor.name: Victron SmartShunt 500A
monitor.why: Same monitor from a van-build specialist.

monitor.name: Victron BMV-712 Smart
monitor.why: Everything the SmartShunt does plus a proper wall screen everyone can glance at.
monitor.downside: Needs a hole cut for the screen.

monitor.name: REDARC Smart Battery Monitor
monitor.why: Best in a REDARC setup, with everything in one app.
monitor.downside: Dearest option, and the screen is extra.
